segments.zh: 好吧，事情是这样的。我一直认为你不仅仅是一个朋友，我再也受不了了。

segments.en: I know you better than anyone. I know the pros and cons of your personality.
segments.zh: 我比任何人都了解你，连你性格的优点和缺点都清楚。

segments.en: I even know what side of the bed is yours. I think we would be great together, don't you?
segments.zh: 我甚至知道床的哪一边是你的。我想我们在一起会很棒，不是吗？

segments.en: Are you serious? We've been friends for years. We can't just change that overnight.
segments.zh: 你是认真的吗？我们多年来一直是朋友，不可能一夜之间就改变这种关系。

segments.en: I know. I never had the guts to tell you until today.
segments.zh: 我知道。 直到今天，我才有勇气告诉你。

segments.en: So what do you say? Are you willing to give me a shot?
segments.zh: 那你怎么说？你愿意给我一次机会吗？

segments.en: Uh, uh...
segments.zh: 嗯嗯……

segments.en: All right, so an interesting dialogue, and it opens up a cultural point.
segments.zh: 好吧，一段有趣的对话，还引出了一个文化话题。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So in the dialogue, the guy was asking her if she would be his girlfriend, right?
segments.zh: 所以在对话中，那个男人问她是否会成为他的女朋友，对吧？

segments.en: Right, but I guess it's not very common, among adults at least, in English-speaking countries.
segments.zh: 对，但我想在英语国家，至少在成年人中，这并不常见。

segments.en: Yeah, we don't say like, okay, so please will you be my boyfriend now?
segments.zh: 是的，我们不说，好吧，请你现在成为我的男朋友吗？

segments.en: Right, right, right.
segments.zh: 对，对，对。

segments.en: You would do that maybe in high school.
segments.zh: 你可能会在高中这样做。

segments.en: Yeah, but even then I think it's still a little funny.
segments.zh: 是的，但即便如此，我还是觉得这仍然有点有趣。

segments.en: I think for us, when we start to have romantic relationships, it just sort of happens naturally, right?
segments.zh: 我想对我们来说，当我们开始有浪漫关系时，它就会自然而然地发生，对吧？

segments.en: You never really have this conversation, will you be my boyfriend?
segments.zh: 你从来不会有这样的对话：你愿意做我的男朋友吗？

segments.en: Right, I guess afterwards you just start talking about other things, which you just consider that you guys are already boyfriend and girlfriend.
segments.zh: 是的，我猜之后你只是开始谈论其他事情，你只是认为你们已经是男朋友和女朋友了。

segments.en: But there's no real... There's no official starting point.
segments.zh: 但没有真正的……没有正式的起点。

segments.en: Yeah, there's no official point that says, okay, now we are boyfriend and girlfriend.
segments.zh: 是的，没有哪个正式的时间点宣布：好，现在我们是男女朋友了。

segments.en: Which is interesting because in other countries they do go through the formality of asking somebody to become their boyfriend.
segments.zh: 这很有趣，因为在其他国家，人们确实会正式地问对方是否愿意做自己的男/女朋友。

segments.en: Yeah, but even, you know, like 20 or 30 years ago in English-speaking countries, you would do this.
segments.zh: 是的，但即使你知道，就像 20 或 30 年前在英语国家一样，你也会这样做。

segments.en: Oh yeah, of course.
segments.zh: 哦，是的，当然。

segments.en: And it was called going steady.
segments.zh: 这在当时叫 going steady（固定交往）。

segments.en: Going steady.
segments.zh: going steady（固定交往）。

segments.en: So you would ask, will you go steady with me?
segments.zh: 所以你会问：你愿意和我固定交往吗？

segments.en: That means let's become a stable couple.
segments.zh: 意思就是成为稳定的情侣。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right, so we want to hear your stories and well, how do you do it in your country?
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们想听听你的故事，好吧，你在你的国家是怎么做的？

segments.en: Do you ask someone out, do you maybe just give them the first kiss and that's an automatic yes?
segments.zh: 你会正式约对方出去，还是直接送上初吻，就算默认答应了？

segments.en: Well, I don't know, but I'm looking forward to hearing from our listeners.
segments.zh: 好吧，我不知道，但我期待着听众的来信。

segments.en: So guys, check out our website EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 所以伙计们，看看我们的网站 englishpod.com。

segments.en: You can leave your questions and comments there.
segments.zh: 您可以将您的问题和评论留在那里。

segments.en: All right, we'll see you guys there and until next time.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们会在那里见到你们，直到下一次。

segments.en: Goodbye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
